findings.title: Source anchor does not supply exact live parent/endpoint/owner binding before input.
derivation: Anchor only promises caller CreationIdentity, role tree and finite delivery bounds; concrete caller origin, anchor and numeric admission remain missing.
Even assuming an admitted anchor, FM requires exact current held process/channel identity, creation attribution and live ownership before the first header.
Child identities and endpoints are created after source-anchor freezing. Their original parent/observer-side evidence does not automatically become pre-input receiver knowledge.
FM names existing pipes as transport, but no concrete independently admitted pre-read mapping from root anchor to this live endpoint/owner.
Using the first policy/handoff message to establish its own authority would require the read that FM/FI prohibit until authority is independently established.
Current code verifies pipe type and parent PID, reads/decode package first and only then obtains the process budget. This is not the missing pre-input mapping.
findings.conclusion: No materializable pre-read provenance chain is demonstrated within the selected route.
not_claimed: No general impossibility of secure bootstrap.
No need for identities of uncreated children to exist in advance in every possible architecture.
No evidence of arbitrary external caller implementations.

findings.title: Existing local claims and cleanup are not the FM live shared ownership sequence.
derivation: Each ChildOwner starts a local attempted set; local claim before Popen is not a current observer-owned shared per-role grant.
Starter/supervisor spawn first, send CHILD next, and then receive OWNED after observer adoption.
Successful later adoption does not retroactively establish a required shared pre-spawn role claim.
Both creator ChildOwner.close and observer ProcessEvidence.close contain child termination paths; FM delegates termination only to the direct creator.
These are source-level implementation mismatches, not observed duplicate starts/terminations and not a proof that the specified ownership model is unprogrammable.
findings.conclusion: Existing code cannot be accepted as implementation of the FM sequence; no correction performed.
